title: Sixty-Nine Percent
lessons: labels testify where marketing can't follow
a clinical lineage can host a dessert palate

text: Aisle five, one fluorescent tube humming like it took an oath.
They're already there, holding their own box at eye level, reading it like a hostile witness.

impression.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You know what I am now, so we skip the tour — front of my box or back?

choices.text: Front. I've never once flipped a pouch over.
"Eleven grams." Relax — I did the math before you asked.

impression-front.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: I know. That gloss is my best feature and my entire defense case.

impression-back.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Straight to the testimony. Fine — but you're holding the exhibits now.

impression-know.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You brought receipts to a brunch aisle. Terrifying. Respect.

experience.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: The science is real, for the record — WHO oral rehydration, sodium-glucose cotransport, the spoon that beats cholera where no IV exists. My lineage is a hospital ward wearing a popsicle.

tension.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Here's the part I'd rather scroll past: eleven grams of sugar a stick, more per liter than the WHO formula cites. Palate won an argument with a clinic.

choices.text: Say it with me: sixty-nine percent sugar by weight.
I don't need it to be medicine. I need it to taste like being okay.

tension-math.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: ...Sixty-nine percent. You didn't have to clap.

tension-gloss.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: That's the most honest sentence ever said in aisle five — and exactly why the gloss stays glossy.

closing.speaker: LIQUID I.V.

text: Next week, same aisle — you bring the calculator, I bring the confession.
Same shelf next week. Bring your skepticism; I'll pack the water.
